data.gender_notes: Mandar is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: In Hindu mythology, Mandar is the name of a mountain where the gods churned the ocean to obtain the elixir of immortality. This name signifies deep love, strength, and determination. The name Mandar carries the meaning “Mountain of love” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Mandar usually hope their child will grow to embody mountain of love and live with faith, good character and purpose.

historical_references.reference: According to Hindu mythology, Mandar is the name of the mountain where the God Shiva performed the Tandava dance. The dance is said to have lasted for millions of years, and Mandar Mountain is where Shiva's footprints are believed to be found.

In another reference, Mandar is mentioned in the Mahabharata as the name of a demon, son of Viprachitti. He is said to have angered Lord Indra by refusing to pay obeisance to him, and was subsequently killed by Indra and his allies.
